rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Businesses, including apartment rental companies, may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (two or more users, using competitor data) as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or coerce users to adopt its price recommendations. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.requirement_es: Las empresas, incluidas las de alquiler de apartamentos, no pueden usar ni distribuir un algoritmo de precios común (con dos o más usuarios que use datos de la competencia) como parte de un acuerdo para restringir la competencia, ni presionar a los usuarios para que adopten sus recomendaciones de precios. Los algoritmos de una sola empresa que usan solo sus propios datos no están cubiertos.
rules.quoted_span: Businesses are expressly prohibited from using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of an agreement to restrain trade.
rules.effective_date_quote: These laws, described below, took effect on January 1, 2026.
rules.key_value: Civil fines up to $1 million; criminal fines up to $6 million (businesses) and $1 million (individuals), per violation
rules.penalty: Civil fines up to $1 million per violation in actions by the Attorney General or a district attorney; criminal fines of the greater of $6 million or twice the gain/loss for corporations and $1 million for individuals.
rules.coverage_conditions: General antitrust law applying to all industries; not specific to rental housing. Applies to common pricing algorithms (two or more users that use competitor data).
rules.exemptions: Proprietary single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data are not covered.
rules.caveat: Secondary source (law firm article); general cross-industry antitrust law that mentions apartment rental companies only as an example, not rental-specific.
